title: Reproduce the granular-layer simulations in Bizon et al. Figure 1
description: Implement the paper's event-driven granular simulation and submit seven normalized trajectory archives reproducing Figure 1.

instructions: Every trajectory must be readable with numpy.load(..., allow_pickle=False) and contain exactly: time (F,), drive_phase (F,), positions (F,N,3), velocities (F,N,3), angular_velocities (F,N,3), diameters (N,), plate_z (F,), plate_vz (F,), and collision_counts (F-1,3).
All arrays must be real numeric arrays. collision_counts must contain nonnegative integers in columns ball_ball, stationary_wall, bottom_plate.
The particle index must identify the same particle in every frame.
Normalize length by mean particle diameter D and acceleration by gravitational acceleration g, so mean diameter and downward gravity both equal 1.
Use a right-handed coordinate system with z increasing upward. positions and plate_z must use the same origin.
Export 4 forcing cycles for a, b, cd, and e; export 8 forcing cycles for f, g, and h.
Record 32 equal phase intervals per cycle, including the initial frame and final endpoint, so F = 32 * exported cycles + 1.
At t=0 the plate is at the midpoint of its oscillation and moving upward. The first frame and each complete-cycle endpoint have drive_phase 0. time must be strictly increasing.
Each case manifest entry must include trajectory, particle_count, box_width, box_height, seed, simulation_cycle, and walltime_seconds. Paths are relative to submission/manifest.json.
